 Thanks to this week's cold front, most of us are waking up to the 50s this morning. 
 Updated: 7:25 AM EST Nov 14, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Sara Blue Meteorologist We are waking up to a fall-like chill in the air on the Gulf Coast. Thanks to this week's cold front, most of us will wake up to the 50s for the first time this season. 
 The last time the mercury dropped to the 50s in Fort Myers was back in April. This morning's chill may be a refreshing shock to the system. 
 Advertisement Your Gulf Coast Weather Most Accurate Forecast shows a cool, crisp day ahead. By the afternoon, high temperatures will only recover to the 60s. Drier air will be in place, too, meaning it won't feel muggy at all across the Gulf Coast.
 Light breezes will stir up a risk of rip currents in Lee and Charlotte counties. A rip current statement is active along some of our beaches through Saturday evening. 
 Gulf Coast News Things get even cooler Sunday morning. Lows will plunge to the 50s and 40s. We will rebound to the 70s under mostly sunny skies Sunday afternoon. 
 Temperatures will recover by next week into the 80s. Low rain chances return Monday, too. 
 In the tropics, no development is expected over the next seven days.
